text.title: API Monitoring Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether a scrape path exists, which layer is still unbuilt (metrics, probes or alerts) and what is already wrong with it, to the one rule that binds the next artefact edit.

decision-tree.root-question: Can this API expose a metrics endpoint scraped by a Prometheus-compatible collector the team controls, or is one agreed to be stood up?

branch.when: no scrape path and none planned; the only telemetry is a managed vendor dashboard the team cannot add series to

conclusion.verdict: skip; without a collector the RED metrics, SLI expressions and burn-rate alerts below have nowhere to live — emit a structured skip naming the missing pipeline

branch.when: a scrape path exists or is committed
branch.question: Which layer is missing: the metrics themselves, the probes, or the alerting on top of them?

branch.when: no RED metrics on this API yet
branch.question: Does the proposed instrumentation label series with the resolved request path, or emit latency as an average or a summary quantile?

branch.when: labels would carry resolved paths, ids, emails or search terms

conclusion.verdict: label on the route template only; state cardinality in the artefact as routes x methods x status-classes before any code lands

branch.when: latency is planned as a summary quantile or an average gauge

conclusion.verdict: switch to a histogram and declare bucket boundaries with an edge at the SLO threshold; list them in the artefact

branch.when: nothing instrumented yet; both the label and the latency shape are still open

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology from the metric list forward; emit the artefact with metric names, probe paths, SLOs and alert rules for review

branch.when: metrics exist and the service runs under an orchestrator that restarts on a failing probe
branch.question: Does the liveness endpoint reach a dependency, and do request logs carry the propagated traceparent?

branch.when: liveness queries the database, cache or an upstream, or one endpoint serves both probes

conclusion.verdict: split the endpoints and strip dependency checks from liveness; a dependency blip must not restart every replica at once

branch.when: probes are clean but log lines carry a locally minted request id

conclusion.verdict: propagate the W3C traceparent trace-id as request_id on every line, so logs and traces key on the same value

branch.when: probes split correctly and logs already carry the propagated trace-id

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology from the SLO section forward; the instrumentation layer is already conformant

branch.when: metrics exist and a human carries a pager for this API
branch.question: Are alerts expressed as burn rate against a target defined as good events over valid events?

branch.when: targets are resource utilisation — CPU, memory, queue depth — not an event ratio

conclusion.verdict: restate each SLO as a PromQL good/valid ratio with target, rolling window and an error budget in absolute failed requests before writing any alert

branch.when: an SLO exists but its alert is a static error-rate threshold

conclusion.verdict: replace with multiwindow burn rate — ~14.4x over 1h with a 5m short window to page, ~6x over 6h with a 30m short window to ticket

branch.when: burn-rate alerts exist but some page rules lack a runbook_url or a for clause longer than the scrape interval

conclusion.verdict: every rule carries severity, a for duration above the scrape interval, and a runbook with at least one diagnostic query; page rules without one are rejected
